sections.overview: The Black Drongo is a widespread resident of tropical South and Southeast Asia, with records extending from southwestern Iran to Indonesia.
sections.identification: It is a glossy black bird about 28 cm long, with a conspicuously broad, deeply forked tail.
sections.habitat: It uses open agricultural country and forest edges, often perching conspicuously on bare branches or utility wires.
sections.diet: Its diet is mainly insects, including grasshoppers, termites, beetles and dragonflies, which it captures around open ground and vegetation.
sections.behavior: The Bangladesh Red List records it as active by day and at twilight.
sections.reproduction: In India, breeding timing varies geographically: it is reported mainly in February and March in the south, and may continue until August elsewhere; both sexes help build a stick cup nest.
sections.ecology: Its insect-eating habits make it a familiar bird of farmland and open habitats; the India assessment reports stable recent annual trend but an inconclusive long-term trend nationally.
sections.conservation: The global Red List category is Least Concern, while the 2025 Indian factsheet notes that national long-term trend estimates remain inconclusive.
